text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The World Bank will extend $12 million to Pakistan to improve and streamline trade and transport administrative procedures and logistics.
- A 10-member Punjab cabinet was sworn in on Monday.
- Punjab governor Khwaja Tariq Rahim resigned.
- The government decided to amend the accountability laws to extend it to high officials.
- President Farooq Leghari promulgated an ordinance imposing curbs on the press.
- A spokesman for President Farooq Leghari described as baseless and frivolous the charges of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto that the president had tapped her home telephone.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the government will try to solve economic problems in the 1997/98 budget (July-June).
- The World Bank has suggested including experienced private sector professionals in the upper management of Pakistan International Airlines to prepare it for privatisation.
- Pakistan and India will discuss the supply of natural gas from various countries to India via Pakistan during their forthcoming talks.
FINANCIAL POST
- The brokerage firm of Yusuf Ismail Nagaria has defaulted on its liabilities to the amount of 40.2 million rupees, says Arif Habib, president of the Karachi Stock Exchange.
THE NATION
- The Lahore High Court ruled by majority decision that a girl can marry a person without the consent of her guardian, allowing Saima Waheed to join her husband.
- Police arrested three senior officers of Faisalabad Development Authority on corruption charges on the orders of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Out-going caretaker Punjab Governor Khawaja Tariq Rahim said the February 3 general elections were not fair and "the ground realities were different from the election results".
